single_node_ceiling.note: Measured single-node limits (HEA-1812). Numbers are hardware-sensitive — see hardware below. Single-node only; multi-node/Raft horizontal scale is a separate axis and is not measured here.
single_node_ceiling.hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS, 16 vCPU, 55 GiB RAM (server + Goose load generator co-resident on one host, loopback)
single_node_ceiling.corpus: resident_corpus=300000 seeded users (realms=5, sessions+revoked per realm), see metadata.dataset_shape
single_node_ceiling.max_comfortable_reason: Last clean steady step: 0 request failures; hot-path journeys (session_lookup / user_lookup / validate) p99 = 1 ms and within budget. The Argon2id-bound issuance/revoke_mint journeys breach their 6 ms HTTP budget by design (password-hash cost), so overall pass=false while the hot path stays sub-ms.
single_node_ceiling.failure_ceiling_reason: Total collapse observed by 1000 concurrent users: 100% request failures, all journeys at 30 s client-timeout. The cliff is between 500u (1664 RPS, clean) and 1000u (100% fail); no clean step exists above 500u. Unthrottled ceiling runs past the knee (6000u) confirm summary.ceiling=server.
single_node_ceiling.reproduction: make loadtest MODE=steady USERS=500 RUN_TIME=45s HATCH_RATE=500  (knee); then USERS=1000 for the cliff. Both against the large demo corpus (make loadtest default). See README § 'Measured single-node ceiling (HEA-1812)'.

metadata.dataset_shape: realms=5 users/realm=80 sessions/realm=40 revoked/realm=4 (sessions_frac=0.5 revoked_frac=0.1 seed=1) resident_corpus=300000

summary.ceiling_reason: a budgeted journey's p99 breached its HTTP budget — server latency is the limiter; the observed ceiling is the server under test
